result.summary:
No numerical bug found in LongHitScorer: every returned key matches an independent brute-force reference, so gp_hit_1 / rl_hit_1 are being paid what the definition says. Two design-level points (orientation rule, sh_* carrying the market's own Sharpe) are worth fixing before the next round, but neither justifies a restart.

What I covered (local only, repo untouched; scratch in /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-wxy-Desktop-230P-hw2/208bbacf-e83a-42e0-b6f4-3ead427e5e95/scratchpad/lh/ — ref.py is the reference, fuzz.py the driver):

- Reference comparison. Plain per-day loops written from the definition, no torch, nothing imported from alphacube. 940 randomized cases (850 with D 6-44 / S 5-69, 90 with S 100-430) plus one at S=5220, both signs, all 44 returned keys with gates off; also production defaults (gates on, both orientations, HIT_WEIGHTS/HIT_SCALES) and score_combined. Tolerance rel 1e-8.
- Inputs used to break it (each alone, then mixed): random NaN in panel and label, whole-day NaN factor (first days, middle days), whole-day NaN label (first, random, last), +-inf in panel and label, float32, days with 0..25 finite names, heavy ties, ties at top or bottom book boundary, labels exactly +-0.0, all-positive / all-negative / all-zero / constant label days, a single labelled name, unbuyable names concentrated in the book, constant-factor days, signed zeros, 1e37-scale values. 22 further degenerate inputs (all-NaN, 1-3 days, 1-5 stocks, int panel) match with no exception.
- Result: zero discrepancies in any LongHitScorer component. The only mismatches (67 of 700 cases, all with a constant-label day) are in ic / lic / long_ic and come from the pre-existing _cs_corr_days_t, not the new code; no weighted long_hit component is affected.
- floor(n*frac) agrees with exact integer floors for every n < 8000 and all four fractions.
- LongScorer after the refactor: same cases against my own reference for its documented definition, both signs and default gates: match (same ic/long_ic caveat). tests/test_long_scorer.py 18 pass.
- PanelScorer: bit-identical to HEAD (HEAD's scoring.py + metrics.py loaded in a separate process): 1952 score records over 122 panels x kind x signed x penalty x gated, plus the raw bytes of rank_ic_turnover and _book_turnover_t.
- Look-ahead (240 perturbation trials, daily series captured by spying on _sharpe_ann): changing day t's label values or NaN pattern changes only day t's net and leaves turnover, to_*, long_tie, long_code, distinct exactly unchanged; changing day t's factor changes only days t and t+1; scoring the first T days reproduces the first T days of the full run exactly.
- Live-days rule: matches for every book (from the first day with a book; no-label days dropped; an all-NaN factor day is an empty book that pays liquidation and re-entry).
- Label exactly 0: counted as a loss under boundary z (strict >), both in the book and in the market base rate, so hit - base stays consistent; for auc it goes in the loser group. With VWAP-ratio labels exact zeros are negligible in production.
- All-up / all-down days: hit_top*, hit_ramp, hit_exp count the day as exactly 0 (not skipped), which shrinks them by the share of such days identically for every factor (half the days all-up: hit_top10_z 0.137 -> 0.067); auc / auc_long skip the day (0.0434 -> 0.0427, equal to the informative days alone). No cross-factor bias, and with about 5000 labelled names such days do not occur.
- Unbuyable names in the book: hold their weight, earn 0, pay turnover, and are excluded from hit denominators — as defined; conservative, not exploitable.
- Performance at (1359, 5220) float32, on a Mac that was heavily loaded by other jobs (load average 16-30), so treat absolute times as upper bounds: long_hit score() 4.0 s wall at 10 threads / 6.4 s CPU single-thread; LongScorer 3.8 s; PanelScorer rank_ic 1.2 s. So about the same cost as the first version and about 3x the old reward. Profile at quarter width: _prepare 41%, _hit_side 44%, _structure 10%. Peak RSS about 1.0 GB (0.5 GB scorer state + 0.3-0.5 GB transient measured; my count of live tensors in _hit_side gives up to about 16 float64 panels = 0.9 GB transient, which memory compression here may have hidden).
- Tests run without writing caches: test_long_hit_scorer.py + test_long_scorer.py 29 passed; test_chain_next, test_label_metrics, test_mining, test_rl_miners, test_tokens_env, test_pool, test_universe_mining 82 passed. The rest of the suite was not run.

issues.what: Orientation is chosen by top-10% GROSS excess, but the fit is made of net top-20% / rank-weighted books plus long-half hit rates and rank IC. When the two ends of a factor differ in turnover or shape, the chosen orientation can have a far lower fit than the other one. It can only under-reward (chosen fit <= max over orientations, which is what the first version takes); it never pays a bad factor more, and it is deterministic and symmetric under negation.
issues.evidence: Constructed case (orient_repro.py, D=1000, S=300, seed 3): f = where(fast in its top 10%, 10 + fast, -slow), both ends predictive. Gross top-10% excess +9.3 bp/day (+1) vs +4.6 (-1), so score() picks +1 with fit -0.0248 (to_top10 0.90, xs_top20 -7.4); orientation -1 has fit +0.0049 (to_top10 0.22). Gap 0.030 = one full fit unit; LongScorer picks -1. Frequency (orient.py, 450 synthetic persistent factors, D=1000, S=300, IC 0 to 0.02, one style factor in returns): lower-fit orientation chosen in 12.9% overall. Excluding the constructed two-speed family: 7.2% (monotone 5.6%, bottom-tail 3.3%, top-tail 6.7%, U-shape 13.3%), but the loss is small: gap > 0.003 in 1.9%, > 0.01 in 0.6%, max 0.013; with true IC >= 0.01 only about 2% are mis-oriented, and 2.8% of the top-20% by best-orientation fit. Two-speed family: 35.6% mis-oriented, gap > 0.01 in 20%, max 0.038 (sample p99 of fit is 0.030). Choosing by net top-10% instead does not help (14.4% overall) because 4 of 6 weight units are gross components. Caveat: synthetic returns, so fit magnitudes are not calibrated to production.
issues.fix: When both orientations pass the tie / code gates, run _hit_side for both and keep the higher fit, as LongScorer does (about +45% per score, since _hit_side is 44% of score()). Before deciding, measure it on the server without touching the runs: score the calibration library or the gp_hit_1 archive leaders with orientations=(1,) and (-1,) and count how many have fit(other) - fit(chosen) > 0.005.

issues.what: sh_top20 and sh_rankw are the portfolio's own Sharpe, so they carry the benchmark's Sharpe over each factor's own live window. Two consequences: (a) fit has a level offset of 0.03 x (0.5/0.43 + 0.5/0.2) / 6 = 0.0183 per 1.0 of market Sharpe, so fit = 0 is not 'no skill' and RL's MIN_SOLO=0 bar is shifted by that amount (laxer if the training-window benchmark Sharpe is positive, stricter if negative); (b) a factor with a longer warm-up starts its live window later and gets a different market Sharpe for free. GP ranking is unaffected by (a); (b) tilts ranking slightly toward long or nested windows if the first months of the sample were a bear market.
issues.evidence: semantics.py, D=1359, S=400, synthetic market with benchmark Sharpe 0.84: a factor that never changes (no skill, no turnover after day 0; xs_top20 -0.05, xs_rankw +0.05) scores fit +0.0158, half of the 0.03 level quoted as the library's 99th percentile. Same factor with its first 120 days set to NaN, in a market whose first 120 days were weak (benchmark Sharpe 0.836 over all days, 0.910 from day 120): fit 0.0304 -> 0.0326, of which about +0.0014 is the two sh_ components (sh_top20 0.916 -> 1.005, sh_rankw 0.830 -> 0.900). Mined expressions use day windows up to 60, nested up to about 120 days, so first-valid days differ by that much. I could not measure the real benchmark path locally.
issues.fix: Report sh_ relative to the benchmark over the same live days: _sharpe_ann(net[live])[0] - _sharpe_ann(self._ew_all[live])[0], then recalibrate the two sh_ scales. Until then, compute the Sharpe of scorer._ew_all on the server over all labelled days and from day 60 / 120; multiply by 0.0183 to get the offset of the MIN_SOLO bar and the size of the warm-up tilt. If the offset is material, set MIN_SOLO to that value for the next RL round instead of 0.

issues.what: A day on which one side is constant at a value that is not exactly representable returns about 0 (or 1e-17) instead of NaN, because the variance is rounding residue rather than exactly 0. The day is then counted as a zero-correlation day in ic / lic / long_ic and as a scored day for the min_scored_days gate. Pre-existing (identical at HEAD), not introduced by this change. No weighted long_hit component is affected: lric uses half-integer ranks, whose mean is exact. LongScorer's long_ic (weight 0.5) is exposed in principle, but a fully tied long half is rejected by the boundary-tie gate.
issues.evidence: _cs_corr_days_t(arange(7)[None], full((1,7), 0.0123)) returns 0.0, and with a constant factor 0.3 against random labels returns 1.46e-17; 0.01, 0.5, 1.0 correctly give NaN. In the fuzz, 67 of 700 cases (all containing a constant-label day) differ from the reference in ic / lic / long_ic, e.g. seed 42, shape (9, 55): ic 0.1125 vs 0.1266. No other key differs in any case.
issues.fix: Use a relative variance threshold, e.g. ok = (n >= MIN_PAIRS) & (va > 1e-20 * n * am*am + tiny) & (same for vb), or test row max == row min over the valid cells. Can wait; in production a whole-day constant label does not occur.

issues.what: The docstring says auc is P(a winner ranks above a loser) - 0.5 and equals half the difference of the two groups' mean u. The mean-u difference itself equals P - 0.5, so the code's auc (0.5 x difference) is half of P - 0.5. Scale only: auc is not in HIT_WEIGHTS and scales are calibrated from the same code, so no reward changes.
issues.evidence: semantics.py section 3: auc_z = 0.16943 while brute-force P(winner above loser) - 0.5 over all pairs = 0.33886, ratio exactly 2.0000. Two-name example: winner on top gives u 0.75 vs 0.25, difference 0.5 = AUC - 0.5, code returns 0.25.
issues.fix: Fix the docstring (auc = (P - 0.5) / 2), or drop the 0.5 factor and double the auc_z / auc_m scales.

issues.what: Two edge behaviours of the live-days rule that match the stated definition but are worth knowing. (1) Trading cost booked on a day with no label at all disappears with the dropped day. (2) The rankw book opens on a day with a single finite name (100% in it), while top5/10/20 and ramp need 2 names and hit rates need 5, so rankw can start one day earlier than the others. Neither matters in production: only the trailing horizon days lack labels, and single-name days do not survive the 0.8 coverage gate in any meaningful number.
issues.evidence: nolabel_cost.py, D=8, S=20, day 3 unlabelled: replacing the book on day 3 charges total turnover 1.0 over the live days (entry only); replacing it on day 4 charges 2.0. With day 0 holding one finite name, live days per book are top5/top10/top20/ramp = 6 and rankw = 7.
issues.fix: Optional: carry the cost of an unlabelled day into the next live day, and require n >= 2 for rankw. Can wait.

issues.what: Passing boundaries= that does not cover a weighted hit component is accepted at construction and then raises KeyError inside composite() on the first score(). Not reachable through make_scorer / the CLI, which never pass boundaries.
issues.evidence: LongHitScorer(y, weights={all components: 1}, scales=..., boundaries=('z',)).score(x) raises KeyError: 'hit_top5_m' (hit while writing nolabel_cost.py).
issues.fix: In __init__, raise ValueError if any weighted hit_ / auc key ends in a boundary not in self.boundaries, or always take the union of the two.
